title: Bouillabaisse
subtitle: Provençal fish stew with saffron and rouille
excerpt: A southern French fish stew built on a saffron and fennel broth, made with a mix of firm white fish and prawns, served over toasted bread spread with garlicky rouille. The great dish of Marseille.

recipe.sourceNotes: Bouillabaisse is the defining dish of Marseille and one of the most disputed dishes in French cooking. The word combines the Provençal words for boil and reduce, describing the technique of fast-boiling the broth to emulsify the oil into it. True Marseillaise bouillabaisse contains specific Mediterranean fish species that are unavailable outside the region: scorpion fish, John Dory, weever, and rascasse among others. Versions made elsewhere use whatever firm, flavourful white fish is available. The essential flavour components are non-negotiable: saffron, fennel, tomato, garlic, orange peel, and a pastis or wine base for the broth. The rouille, a rust-coloured garlic and saffron mayonnaise, is spread on the croutons and floated on top of the soup.

content.text: The broth is made first and strained, then the fish is poached directly in it for serving. The broth should be intensely flavoured: taste and reduce it further if it seems weak before adding the fish. Add the fish in order of thickness: the largest, firmest pieces go in first. The soup is traditionally served in two courses: the broth with croutons and rouille first, then the fish on a separate plate.

Heat the olive oil in a large pot. Fry the onion and fennel for 10 minutes. Add 4 cloves of garlic and cook for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, wine, saffron water, orange peel, thyme, bay leaves, and 800 ml of water. Simmer for 20 minutes. Season with salt.
Blend the broth until smooth and pass through a sieve, pressing well. Return to the pan and bring back to a simmer. Taste: it should be intense. Reduce further if needed.
Make the rouille: crush the remaining 2 cloves of garlic to a paste with a pinch of salt. Stir into the mayonnaise with the cayenne and a pinch of saffron. Set aside.

Add the cod and salmon to the simmering broth. Cook for 3 minutes. Add the mussels and prawns. Cover and cook for a further 3 to 4 minutes until the mussels are open and the prawns are pink. Discard any mussels that have not opened. Serve the broth with toasted bread spread with rouille, then the fish separately.
